title: Control and Coordination
subject: Biology
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET / NEET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Neuron Structure, Types & Neuroglial Cells
points: Neuron structure: Cyton / Soma (cell body with Nissl's granules of rough ER/ribosomes, neurofibrils), Dendrites (short, branched, afferent), Axon (single long efferent process originating at Axon hillock; covered by myelin sheath interrupted by Nodes of Ranvier). Synaptic knobs contain neurotransmitter vesicles.
Neuron types: Unipolar (embryonic stage), Bipolar (retina of eye, olfactory epithelium), Multipolar (cerebral cortex, most common). Sensory (afferent), Motor (efferent), Interneurons.

Neuroglia (supporting glial cells): Astrocytes (form blood-brain barrier), Oligodendrocytes (form myelin sheath in CNS), Schwann cells (form myelin sheath in PNS), Microglia (phagocytic scavengers), Ependymal cells (line brain ventricles, circulate CSF).

formulas.label: Neuron structural polarity
formulas.expr: Dendrites (receive signals toward soma) → Soma / Cyton → Axon hillock → Axon → Synaptic knobs (efferent)

formulas.label: Myelination agents distinction
formulas.expr: PNS Myelin = Schwann cells | CNS Myelin = Oligodendrocytes

nodes.title: Conduction of Nerve Impulse: Resting & Action Potential
points: 1. Resting Membrane Potential (Polarized State, −70 mV): Axolemma is more permeable to K⁺ than Na⁺; active Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase pump extrudes 3 Na⁺ for every 2 K⁺ pumped in using 1 ATP, maintaining internal negativity.
2. Action Potential (Depolarization, +30 mV): Threshold stimulus (−55 mV) opens voltage-gated Na⁺ channels causing massive Na⁺ influx, reversing polarity to +30 mV (Spike potential).
3. Repolarization: Na⁺ channels close; voltage-gated K⁺ channels open causing rapid K⁺ efflux, restoring internal negativity.
4. Hyperpolarization: K⁺ channels stay open longer, dropping potential to −80 mV before Na⁺/K⁺ pump restores resting −70 mV.
Saltatory Conduction: In myelinated neurons, action potential jumps from one Node of Ranvier to next; 50-100 times faster (~120 m/s vs 1-2 m/s in unmyelinated fibers).

formulas.label: Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase pump stoichiometry
formulas.expr: Pumps 3 Na⁺ OUT : 2 K⁺ IN (requires 1 ATP; maintains resting membrane potential −70 mV)

formulas.label: Membrane potential phases values
formulas.expr: Resting: −70 mV | Threshold: −55 mV | Peak Action Potential: +30 mV | Hyperpolarization: −80 to −90 mV

formulas.label: Saltatory conduction speed advantage
formulas.expr: Myelinated nerve = 100 - 120 m/s (Saltatory) vs Non-myelinated nerve = 1 - 2 m/s (Continuous)

nodes.title: Synaptic Transmission & Reflex Action
points: Chemical Synapse: Action potential reaching presynaptic terminal opens voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels → Ca²⁺ influx causes synaptic vesicles to exocytose neurotransmitters (Acetylcholine, Noradrenaline) into 20-30 nm synaptic cleft → bind postsynaptic ligand-gated receptors → generates EPSP (depolarization) or IPSP (hyperpolarization by GABA opening Cl⁻ channels).
Electrical Synapse: Gap junctions allow direct ionic current flow; faster but rare in humans.
Reflex Action: Involuntary, automatic, instantaneous motor response to a sensory stimulus without prior brain consultation.
Reflex Arc sequence: Receptor organ → Sensory neuron (enters via dorsal root) → Interneuron in spinal cord grey matter → Motor neuron (exits via ventral root) → Effector organ (muscle/gland).

formulas.label: Chemical synaptic sequence
formulas.expr: Action potential → Ca²⁺ influx → Neurotransmitter exocytosis into cleft → Receptor binding → Postsynaptic ion influx

formulas.label: Neurotransmitter types matching
formulas.expr: Excitatory: Acetylcholine, Glutamate, Noradrenaline | Inhibitory: GABA (γ-aminobutyric acid), Glycine

formulas.label: Reflex arc components pathway
formulas.expr: Receptor → Sensory neuron (Dorsal root) → Interneuron (Grey matter) → Motor neuron (Ventral root) → Effector

nodes.title: Human Central Nervous System: Forebrain, Midbrain & Hindbrain
points: Meninges: Duramater (outer thick), Arachnoid (middle web-like, CSF in subarachnoid space), Piamater (inner vascular).

1. Forebrain: Cerebrum (80% brain weight; hemispheres connected by Corpus callosum, unique to mammals; 4 lobes: Frontal motor/Broca's speech, Parietal sensory/gustatory, Temporal auditory/Wernicke's, Occipital visual); Thalamus (sensory relay station); Hypothalamus (thermoregulation, hunger, thirst, controls pituitary); Limbic system (emotional brain, amygdala, hippocampus for memory).
2. Midbrain: Corpora quadrigemina (superior colliculi for visual reflexes, inferior colliculi for auditory reflexes); Aqueduct of Sylvius.

3. Hindbrain: Cerebellum (Arbor vitae; balance, posture, fine voluntary muscle coordination); Pons (pneumotaxic center); Medulla Oblongata (vital centers: cardiac, vasomotor, respiratory rhythm, vomiting, swallowing).

formulas.label: Mammalian brain hallmark
formulas.expr: Corpus callosum (thick transversal band of white fibers connecting left and right cerebral hemispheres)

formulas.label: Hindbrain functional centers
formulas.expr: Cerebellum = Balance & equilibrium (Arbor vitae) | Medulla = Cardiac, vasomotor, vomiting centers | Pons = Pneumotaxic

nodes.title: Spinal Cord, Peripheral & Autonomic Nervous System
points: Spinal Cord: Extends from foramen magnum to L1-L2; central canal contains CSF; 'H'-shaped inner grey matter surrounded by outer white matter.

PNS Nerves: Cranial nerves (12 pairs: I Olfactory, II Optic, VIII Auditory sensory; III, IV, VI, XI, XII motor; V Trigeminal largest, X Vagus longest mixed nerve); Spinal nerves (31 pairs: 8C, 12T, 5L, 5S, 1Co; ALL spinal nerves are MIXED!).

Autonomic Nervous System (ANS): 1) Sympathetic (Thoracolumbar outflow, Noradrenaline): 'Fight or flight' (dilates pupils, accelerates heart, dilates bronchi, inhibits gut); 2) Parasympathetic (Craniosacral outflow, Acetylcholine): 'Rest and digest' (constricts pupils, slows heart, stimulates digestion).

formulas.label: Human nerve counts
formulas.expr: Cranial nerves = 12 pairs | Spinal nerves = 31 pairs (8C + 12T + 5L + 5S + 1Co; all mixed)

formulas.label: Autonomic nervous system antagonism
formulas.expr: Sympathetic (Thoracolumbar, Noradrenaline, Stress 'Fight/Flight') vs Parasympathetic (Craniosacral, Acetylcholine, 'Rest/Digest')

nodes.title: Sensory Receptors: Eye & Ear Anatomy and Function
points: 1. Human Eye: Sclera (cornea anteriorly); Choroid (ciliary body, iris with pupil); Retina: Rods (rhodopsin, twilight vision) and Cones (iodopsin, color/photopic vision); Fovea centralis / Macula lutea (only cones, point of highest visual acuity); Blind spot (lacks photoreceptors, optic nerve exits).

2. Human Ear: External ear (pinna, auditory canal); Middle ear (tympanic membrane, 3 Ear Ossicles: Malleus, Incus, Stapes smallest bone amplifying sound 20×; Eustachian tube equalizes pressure); Inner ear (Labyrinth):
- Cochlea (Hearing): Organ of Corti on basilar membrane with hair cells.
- Vestibular apparatus (Equilibrium): Crista ampullaris in semicircular canals (dynamic balance/rotation); Maculae in utricle and saccule (static balance/gravity).

formulas.label: Ear ossicles amplification chain
formulas.expr: Malleus (Hammer) → Incus (Anvil) → Stapes (Stirrup, oval window); amplifies sound pressure ~20 times

formulas.label: Equilibrium sensors in inner ear
formulas.expr: Dynamic / Angular equilibrium = Crista ampullaris | Static / Linear equilibrium = Macula (Utricle & Saccule)

nodes.title: Endocrine Glands: Pituitary, Thyroid & Adrenal Glands
points: Pituitary (Hypophysis): Adenohypophysis secretes GH (Gigantism/Acromegaly in hyper, Dwarfism in hypo), TSH, ACTH, PRL, FSH, LH; Neurohypophysis stores Oxytocin (birth, milk let-down) and ADH / Vasopressin (water reabsorption; hyposecretion causes Diabetes Insipidus).

Thyroid Gland: Secretes T₄, T₃ (requires iodine; regulates BMR) and Thyrocalcitonin (TCT, lowers blood Ca²⁺). Hypothyroidism causes Goitre, Cretinism (infants), Myxedema (adults); Hyperthyroidism causes Graves' disease.
Parathyroid Glands: Secretes Parathormone (PTH / Collip's hormone: elevates blood Ca²⁺ by bone resorption; antagonistic to Calcitonin!).

Adrenal Glands: Adrenal Cortex secretes Aldosterone (Na⁺ balance), Cortisol (glucocorticoid, anti-inflammatory), Sex corticoids; Adrenal Medulla secretes Adrenaline & Noradrenaline (3F emergency hormones).

formulas.label: Calcium homeostasis antagonistic hormones
formulas.expr: Calcitonin (Thyroid) lowers blood Ca²⁺ ⇌ Parathormone / PTH (Parathyroid) raises blood Ca²⁺

formulas.label: Diabetes Insipidus etiology
formulas.expr: Hyposecretion of ADH (Vasopressin) → Excessive dilute urination (Polyuria) & excessive thirst (Polydipsia)

nodes.title: Pancreas, Gonads & Mechanism of Hormone Action
points: Pancreas (Islets of Langerhans): α-cells secrete Glucagon (hyperglycemic; glycogenolysis); β-cells secrete Insulin (hypoglycemic; stimulates glucose uptake; deficiency causes Diabetes Mellitus); δ-cells secrete Somatostatin.
Gonadal hormones: Testes secrete Testosterone (Leydig cells); Ovaries secrete Estrogen (follicles) and Progesterone (corpus luteum).
Mechanisms of Hormone Action:

1. Peptide / Protein Hormones (Hydrophilic: Insulin, FSH, Adrenaline): Bind extracellular membrane receptors → activate adenylate cyclase → generate Secondary Messengers (cAMP, IP₃, Ca²⁺) → biochemical response cascade.

2. Steroid & Thyroid Hormones (Lipophilic: Estrogen, Cortisol, Thyroxine): Diffuse across membrane → bind Intracellular nuclear receptors → Hormone-receptor complex binds DNA / HRE, directly altering gene expression.

formulas.label: Glucose homeostasis antagonistic hormones
formulas.expr: Insulin (β-cells) lowers blood glucose ⇌ Glucagon (α-cells) raises blood glucose

formulas.label: Secondary messengers in peptide hormone action
formulas.expr: cAMP (cyclic AMP), IP₃ (inositol trisphosphate), DAG (diacylglycerol), Ca²⁺

formulas.label: Lipophilic steroid mechanism
formulas.expr: Steroid Hormone + Intracellular Nuclear Receptor → Hormone-Receptor Complex → Direct Gene Transcription

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Reflex Arc
points: Board Q1: Describe the structure of a multipolar neuron with a neat labelled diagram.
Board Q2: Explain the conduction of nerve impulse along an unmyelinated nerve fiber (polarization, depolarization, repolarization).
Board Q3: Explain the structure and functions of Cerebrum, Cerebellum, and Medulla oblongata.
Board Q4: Mechanism of action of peptide hormones (cAMP secondary messenger) vs steroid hormones (nuclear receptor).
Board Q5: Compare Diabetes Mellitus (insulin deficiency, high blood glucose) vs Diabetes Insipidus (ADH deficiency, dilute polyuria).

formulas.label: Diabetes Mellitus vs Insipidus comparison
formulas.expr: Mellitus = Insulin deficiency (High blood glucose + sugar in urine) | Insipidus = ADH deficiency (Dilute polyuria, normal glucose)

formulas.label: Thyroid hyposecretion disorders
formulas.expr: Cretinism (in infants: dwarfism + mental retardation) | Myxedema / Gull's disease (in adults: puffiness, low BMR)

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Conduction velocity: Saltatory conduction in myelinated axons (~120 m/s) is ~50-100 times faster than continuous conduction in unmyelinated fibers (~1-2 m/s).
TRAP 2: Longest cranial nerve vs Largest: Vagus (CN X) is the LONGEST cranial nerve; Trigeminal (CN V) is the LARGEST cranial nerve.
TRAP 3: Calcium regulating hormones: Calcitonin LOWERS blood Ca²⁺ (bone deposition); Parathormone (PTH) ELEVATES blood Ca²⁺ (bone resorption).
TRAP 4: Insulin vs Glucagon: Insulin is HYPOGLYCEMIC (lowers blood sugar); Glucagon is HYPERGLYCEMIC (raises blood sugar).
TRAP 5: Corpus callosum: Present ONLY in mammalian brain; connects right and left cerebral hemispheres.

formulas.label: Cranial nerves superlatives
formulas.expr: Longest = CN X (Vagus) | Largest = CN V (Trigeminal) | Smallest = CN VI (Abducens) / CN IV (Trochlear)

formulas.label: Hormone classification by solubility
formulas.expr: Hydrophilic (Membrane receptor + cAMP): Peptides, Adrenaline | Lipophilic (Nuclear receptor): Steroids, Thyroxine

formulas.label: Mammalian brain diagnostic marker
formulas.expr: Presence of Corpus callosum and Corpora quadrigemina
